deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from p.239). Euler wants rationals a, b, c with abc(a+b+c) = 1. Such a triple gives (p^2-q^2)(q^2-r^2) = biquadrate through q = a+b, r = a-b, p = a+b+2c. He writes a = x/s, b = y/s, c = z/s, so the condition becomes xyz(x+y+z) = s^4. He imposes s^4 = (x+y+z)^2 p^2. Then xyz = (x+y+z)p^2, so z = (x+y)p^2/(xy-p^2), x+y+z = xy(x+y)/(xy-p^2), and s^2 = (x+y+z)p = xyp(x+y)/(xy-p^2). (Modern remark, mine: with sides y+z, z+x, x+y, Heron's formula gives area^2 = xyz(x+y+z). So the problem is a rational triangle whose area is a rational square.)

THIS PAGE.
(1) Put x = n q^2, y = n r^2. Then xy = n^2q^2r^2 and x+y = n(q^2+r^2), so s^2 = n^3 q^2 r^2 p (q^2+r^2)/(n^2q^2r^2 - p^2). Equivalently s^2/(n^2q^2r^2) = n p (q^2+r^2)/(n^2q^2r^2 - p^2).
(2) Put nqr - p = k(q^2+r^2), i.e. p = nqr - k(q^2+r^2). Implicit step (mine): n^2q^2r^2 - p^2 = (nqr-p)(nqr+p) = k(q^2+r^2)(2nqr - k(q^2+r^2)). Hence s^2/(n^2q^2r^2) = n(nqr - k(q^2+r^2))/(k(2nqr - k(q^2+r^2))) = n(k(q^2+r^2) - nqr)/(k(k(q^2+r^2) - 2nqr)). This must be a rational square.
(3) Casus I, n = 2k. Euler writes the ratio as (q^2+r^2-2qr)/(q^2+r^2-4qr) = (q-r)^2/(q^2+r^2-4qr). He therefore requires q^2+r^2-4qr = square.
- He sets the root to q + (f/g)r and divides by r: g^2 r - 4g^2 q = 2fgq + f^2 r. Hence q/r = (g^2-f^2)/(4g^2+2fg), and he takes q = g^2-f^2, r = 4g^2+2fg.
- Then s/(nqr) = (q-r)/(q+(f/g)r) = (3g^2+f^2+2fg)/(g^2+f^2+4fg), up to sign.
- So s = 2k(g^2-f^2)(4g^2+2fg)(3g^2+f^2+2fg)/(g^2+f^2+4fg).
- Further p = 2kqr - k(q^2+r^2) = -k(q-r)^2, x = 2kq^2, y = 2kr^2, z = (x+y)p^2/(xy-p^2).
(4) Casus II, n = k. The ratio is (q^2+r^2-qr)/(q-r)^2, so q^2-qr+r^2 must be a square.
- Root q + (f/g)r gives g^2 r - g^2 q = 2fgq + f^2 r. Hence q/r = (g^2-f^2)/(g^2+2fg); take q = g^2-f^2, r = g^2+2fg.
- Then s/(kqr) = (q+(f/g)r)/(q-r) = (g^2+fg+f^2)/(f^2+2fg) in absolute value (the true value is negative).
- Also p = k(qr - q^2 - r^2), x = kq^2, y = kr^2, z = (x+y)p^2/(xy-p^2).
(5) Aliter. Write s^2 = p(x+y)/(1 - p^2/(xy)) and choose p = 2xy/(x+y). Then 1 - p^2/(xy) = (x-y)^2/(x+y)^2, so s^2 = 2xy(x+y)^2/(x-y)^2. It remains to make 2xy a square: take x = 2q^2, y = r^2.
- This gives s = 2qr(2q^2+r^2)/(2q^2-r^2) and p = 4q^2r^2/(2q^2+r^2).
- It also gives z = p^2(2q^2+r^2)/(2q^2r^2-p^2) = 8q^2r^2(2q^2+r^2)/(2q^2-r^2)^2.
- Implicit check (mine): x+y+z = (2q^2+r^2)^3/(2q^2-r^2)^2 and (x+y+z)p = s^2 exactly. So this is a genuine two-parameter family with abc(a+b+c) = 1:
  a = q(2q^2-r^2)/(r(2q^2+r^2)), b = r(2q^2-r^2)/(2q(2q^2+r^2)), c = 4qr/(2q^2-r^2).
- For q = r = 1 this gives (a,b,c) = (1/3, 1/6, 4), which yields p:q:r = 51:3:1 of p.239, since (51^2-9)(9-1) = 12^4.
(6) Exemplum casus primi, g = 2, f = 1.
- q = 3, r = 20 (q^2+r^2-4qr = 169 = 13^2).
- s = 2*3*20*17k/13, p = 17^2 k (true value -17^2 k), x = 18k, y = 800k.
- z = 818*17^4 k^3/(409*13^2 k^2) = 2*17^4 k/13^2 (true value negative).
- a = 3*13/(17*20), b = 13*20/(3*17), c = 17^3/(3*13*20), with abc = 13*17/(3*20).
- Euler finds that a+b+c is not 60/221 and writes 'falsa!'. The cause is the slip in Casus I (see errors).
errors: Casus I: with n = 2k the ratio n(k(q^2+r^2)-nqr)/(k(k(q^2+r^2)-2nqr)) equals 2(q-r)^2/(q^2+r^2-4qr), not (q-r)^2/(q^2+r^2-4qr). Euler dropped the factor n/k = 2. This is exactly why the example comes out 'falsa'. With his s one gets xyz(x+y+z) = 4 s^4, i.e. abc(a+b+c) = 4, not 1.

Correctly done, Casus I needs 2(q^2-4qr+r^2) = square, i.e. X^2 - 3Y^2 = 2W^2 with X = q-2r, Y = r. Reducing mod 3 shows this has only the trivial solution. So Casus I yields nothing at all, not merely a computational slip.

Signs in Casus I: p = -k(q-r)^2. In the example xy - p^2 = 14400k^2 - 83521k^2 < 0, so z = -2*17^4 k/13^2 and c = -17^3/(3*13*20) are negative. Euler writes them positive. With correct signs a+b+c = -240/221 and abc(a+b+c) = (-221/60)(-240/221) = 4.

Casus II is algebraically correct but always gives xy - p^2 = -k^2(q^2+r^2)(q-r)^2 < 0. Hence z = -k(q^2-qr+r^2)^2/(q-r)^2 < 0 and x+y+z < 0. It gives rational but not positive solutions; Euler does not remark on this.
Minor: Euler's displayed s/(kqr) = (g^2+fg+f^2)/(f^2+2fg) and s/(nqr) in Casus I omit an overall minus sign. This is harmless because only s^2 matters.

results.what: Reduction of abc(a+b+c) = 1 (equivalently xyz(x+y+z) = s^4) via s^2 = (x+y+z)p and x = nq^2, y = nr^2, p = nqr - k(q^2+r^2), to a conic condition
results.modern_name: Rational triangles (Heron triangles) with square area; quartic surface xyz(x+y+z) = w^4 parametrized by reduction to conics
results.usually_credited_to: Rational/Heron triangle problems go back to Diophantus/Brahmagupta; triangles with square area treated in 19th-20th c. literature (Dickson, History vol. II, ch. on rational triangles)

results.what: Casus II: q^2 - qr + r^2 = square parametrized by q = g^2 - f^2, r = g^2 + 2fg, giving a two-parameter (non-positive) family
results.modern_name: Rational parametrization of a conic by a line through a known point (chord method)

results.what: Aliter: choice p = 2xy/(x+y), x = 2q^2, y = r^2 gives the explicit positive family a = q(2q^2-r^2)/(r(2q^2+r^2)), b = r(2q^2-r^2)/(2q(2q^2+r^2)), c = 4qr/(2q^2-r^2) with abc(a+b+c) = 1; the case q = r = 1 gives (51,3,1) with (p^2-q^2)(q^2-r^2) = 12^4
results.modern_name: Parametric family of rational points on abc(a+b+c) = 1 / triangles with square area / (p^2-q^2)(q^2-r^2) = biquadrate
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (fragment printed in Opera Postuma 1862); related problems in Dickson's History

deep.surprise_reason: Routine Eulerian Diophantine manipulation (substitutions plus conic parametrization), already printed in the 1862 Opera Postuma. The page contains a slip (lost factor 2) that Euler himself flagged as 'falsa'. The Aliter family is a neat explicit parametrization but not a result attributed to anyone later.
